summary: M3.16 axc rewrite-verify is a correct, adversary-resistant differential verifier. I read rewrite_verify.rs (1272 LOC), the MCP tool, the CLI handler, the reused helpers (within_ulp_f32/seeded_inputs/derive_workgroups), and the runtime dispatch/readback contract line-by-line, re-ran the 24 core unit tests + 6 CLI integration tests (all green), independently drove the CLI across REJECT/ERROR/FAIL/preflight paths (exit codes and closed taxonomy exactly match spec Section 5), and byte-diffed the saxpy vs saxpy_reassoc SPIR-V (24 localized bytes differ in the arithmetic region — the ACCEPT fixture is genuinely a distinct rewrite, not a self-compare). Every interface-cheat vector I attacked is gated; every comparator errs in the SAFE direction (false-reject, never false-bless); the determinism self-check is correctly ordered BEFORE candidate judgment; and I found NO panic path that escapes the closed verdict taxonomy. The findings below are all non-blocking warnings / design-level caveats, none of which can cause a wrong rewrite to be silently blessed.

warnings.description: The Relative comparator floors its denominator at REL_TINY=1e-8 (denom = max(|a|,|b|,1e-8)). For an output element that lands near zero (e.g. saxpy alpha*x+y catastrophic cancellation), a tiny ~1-ULP absolute perturbation reads as a huge relative error, so rel:EPS can FALSE-FAIL a legitimately-equivalent rewrite at that element. This is why AT-2855 must PIN seed=1 (documented: seed=0 hits worst_max_rel 6.6e-3, seed=1 gives 6.8e-5). IMPORTANT: this errs in the SAFE direction — it can reject a valid rewrite, it can NEVER bless a wrong one — and it matches the DESIGN.md Section 510 relative form the frozen Q4_K_M oracle already uses, so it is spec-sanctioned, not a defect. The seed pin is a test-reliability workaround, not a masking hack (the bit-exact FAIL leg still asserts n_diff>0 and was observed to FAIL on NVIDIA+Lavapipe). Flagging as a robustness caveat of the rel: mode for a future condition-aware tolerance; routes to Architect, not Coder.

The reused within_ulp_f32 (and rewrite_verify's mirroring ulp_diff_f32) computes bit distance as abs_diff of the raw to_bits reinterpreted as i32, WITHOUT the two's-complement monotonic normalization. Across a true sign boundary (small -x vs small +x that are not ==) it reports a near-2^31 ULP distance, i.e. a false mismatch. NaN is handled correctly (returns false = mismatch, no NaN laundering) and -0.0==+0.0 short-circuits true via the a==b check. Again this errs SAFE (false-FAIL only) and the helper is reused verbatim per the spec's reuse map, not newly authored. Minor pre-existing-helper caveat.

The end-to-end MCP override test at_2849_verify_rewrite_tolerance_overridden_stamp_on_lavapipe and the Lavapipe-runnable accept tests use an env-gated EARLY-RETURN soft skip (if AXC_ENABLE_GPU_TESTS != 1 { return; }) rather than #[ignore]. Under a plain `cargo test` with no GPU env they PASS VACUOUSLY. This matches the existing at_1114/at_1115 precedent in the same file and they DO exercise handle() end-to-end on Lavapipe CI. NOTE: contrary to the QA report's 'no automated test invokes handle() end-to-end' framing, this test DOES drive the real verify_rewrite MCP handler through the dispatch path and asserts tolerance_overridden==true + the tolerance_loosened_by_caller note (and the false converse) — the coverage exists, it is merely env-gated rather than #[ignore]-gated. Not blocking.

Output buffers whose element type is neither f32 nor f16 fall back to raw-byte BitExact compare even when the request asked for Ulp/Relative, with a `notes` annotation. This is STRICTER than requested (safe direction — cannot bless a wrong rewrite) and is exactly the documented Section 3.3 v1 fallback. Noted for completeness.

adversarial_checks.interface_gate_bypass_hunt: PASS — read diff_interface line-by-line. Buffer count/name/elem-type/buffer_position/access all gated per position (buffer_position folded into buffer_type sub-kind, spec-consistent). A same-typed buffer ORDER swap is caught by BufferName (names differ per position; names are unique so cannot collude). All THREE BufferAccess variants (ReadOnly/ReadWrite/WriteOnly) compared via enum != — output-aliasing cheat (WriteOnly->ReadWrite, ReadOnly->ReadWrite) caught (verified by at_2848b). Scalars gated on name+ty+offset+member_index, so push-constant TYPE layout is gated (not merely total byte length); push_constant_total_bytes gated separately. workgroup_size compared as full [u32;3] (all 3 dims). coopmat shape / shared_memory_bytes / kernel_name INTENTIONALLY ungated — I confirmed the justification holds in code: any observable numeric consequence of a coopmat/shared change is caught by the differential compare (different output => FAIL), and shared-over-limit is caught at dispatch preflight (typed_rewritten_fail => FAIL/preflight_fail_rewritten). No un-gated field can silently change observable behavior without the differential catching it.
adversarial_checks.comparator_correctness: PASS — BitExact is a true per-element to_bits() byte compare (f32) / raw-u16 compare (f16, avoiding f32-promotion collapse). Relative denominator is eps-floored at 1e-8 (division-by-tiny is guarded, see W1). Ulp reuses within_ulp_f32 (see W2). NaN: BitExact passes only on bit-identical NaN payloads (correct); Relative explicitly guards !is_nan on both operands => NaN FAILs; Ulp returns false for NaN => FAILs. No NaN-laundering path exists. ulp_diff_f32 returns u32::MAX sentinel for NaN and is correctly excluded from max_ulp tracking without affecting the pass/fail decision.
adversarial_checks.determinism_self_check_ordering: PASS — verify_rewrite dispatches the ORIGINAL twice (run1, run2) with byte-identical inputs/grid/push-constants BEFORE the rewritten kernel is ever prepared (step 8 follows step 7 in source order, lines 811-852). find_nondeterminism byte-compares run1 vs run2 and yields NONDETERMINISTIC_ORACLE. An infra error in the SECOND original dispatch cannot masquerade as nondeterminism: it routes to typed_original_skip => SKIPPED, not NondeterministicOracle. The differential compare uses run1 (the first original run), not run2. Empirically confirmed by QA AT-2860 (no spurious verdict for saxpy-vs-itself, which only holds because dispatch re-uploads inputs each call, resetting the in-place ReadWrite y buffer — verified against the runtime dispatch contract).
adversarial_checks.fill_implementation: PASS — [-1,1] map v=(u as f64 / u32::MAX)*2-1 is inclusive-bounds, denormal/NaN/Inf-free (unit test build_inputs_float_buffers_are_finite_and_in_range confirms). Per-buffer seed is seed^b for both f32 fill and the integer path (build_inputs passes seed^b to seeded_inputs, whose internal ^0 leaves it seed^b — no double-XOR bug). Original and rewritten receive BYTE-IDENTICAL inputs: build_inputs is called ONCE (from meta_orig.binding_plan, whose buffer element types the interface gate already proved equal to meta_rewritten) and the same Vec is reused for all three dispatches. f16 path rounds the same [-1,1] f32 draw via half::f16::from_f32.
adversarial_checks.panic_taxonomy_escape: PASS — traced every indexing site. buffer_sizes[b] guarded by an explicit len()==buffers.len() check before build_inputs. Comparators index a[i*4..] up to sz where sz=output_sizes[i]; the runtime readback_from_persistent_mapping returns EXACTLY out_size bytes for every readback binding and an empty Vec for ReadOnly/zero-size bindings, and compare_outputs skips ReadOnly and sz==0 bindings, so no comparator indexes past a returned buffer. run1/run2/run_rewritten all have len==binding_plan.buffers.len() (dispatch validates and pushes one entry per binding). serde_json failures are handled with unwrap_or_else fallback strings. No panic path escapes the closed 6-value verdict set.
adversarial_checks.mcp_layer: PASS — resolve_source path-resolution is identical to the existing bench_variant/compile_variant precedent (arbitrary .axc file read is the established MCP contract, not a new vuln). Tolerance is server-owned-default BitExact via default_bit_exact; ANY non-BitExact caller policy sets tolerance_overridden=true + a tolerance_loosened_by_caller note unconditionally (line 91, 118-121) — a silent loosening on the agent-driven path is impossible and the stamp is supervisor-audited (pipeline rule #3). A malformed tolerance string => InvalidParams (-32602); oversized/invalid base64 => InvalidParams; wrong-length push-constants => ERROR/preflight/infra_error. Vulkan-unavailable => hard RPC error -32004 (documented divergence from the CLI's SKIPPED).
adversarial_checks.spirv_spot_check: PASS — compiled examples/saxpy.axc and examples/saxpy_reassoc.axc to SPIR-V; both are 1308 bytes and differ in exactly 24 bytes clustered in the arithmetic (OpFMul/OpFAdd + consequent SSA renumbering) region. Confirms saxpy_reassoc is a GENUINE distinct rewrite (single commutative operand swap yi+alpha*xi vs alpha*xi+yi), so the AT-2859 bit-exact ACCEPT is non-vacuous (the harness dispatches two different kernels and compares outputs), not a same-source self-compare. spirv-dis was unavailable in-environment; byte-diff substituted.
adversarial_checks.test_integrity: PASS — AT-2853/2855 reject fixtures assert n_diff>0 as the non-vacuity guard (rewrite_verify_gpu.rs:317, 395). AT-2855's alpha=0 leg is explicitly LABELED a negative control inside the reject-tolerance test and asserted PASS (proving the pinned alpha=2.0 is load-bearing); it is NOT counted as an accept fixture. The at_1115 pre-existing Lavapipe reference genuinely predates this branch (git: originates in commit 26e095b, confirmed an ancestor of main; bench_variant is touched by this diff ONLY for the within_ulp_f32 pub(crate) promotion, a no-logic-change verified by git diff). No test passes vacuously in a way that hides a defect (the env-gated soft-skips of W3 run for real on Lavapipe CI).

scope_isolation_check: PASS (no changes under axc-lexer/parser/hir/mir/codegen; bench_variant change is the within_ulp_f32 pub(crate) promotion only; compiler crates untouched as spec mandates)

independent_verification.cli_driven_manually: REJECT->exit1/stage=interface/sub=buffer_count; ERROR(garbage --tol)->exit2/infra_error; ERROR(missing file)->exit2; ERROR(float-scalar no push-constants)->exit2/preflight/push_constants_required; FAIL(non-compiling rewritten)->exit1/compile_fail_rewritten/side=rewritten. Taxonomy and exit codes match spec Section 5 exactly.
independent_verification.spirv_bytediff: saxpy.spv vs reassoc.spv: 24/1308 bytes differ, localized to arithmetic region
